commit.message:
fix(B): send host keys to the open screen instead of queueing them for the game

"key" always bumped KeyMapping.clickCount, even with a screen open. In 26.3
Minecraft.tick runs handleKeybinds only when no screen is open, and
KeyMapping.releaseAll only runs when a screen opens, so those clicks stayed
queued and fired as soon as the screen closed: E in an inventory did nothing
(only a screen's keyPressed closes it), then Esc closed it and the next tick
reopened it; Q dropped the held item later.

With a screen open, "key" down and "slot" now build a KeyEvent the way
KeyboardHandler does (scancode from the mapping's bound key, keycode via
SDL_GetKeyFromScancode, so the default swap key does not look like Tab) and call
screen.keyPressed, never touching clickCount or setDown. E closes a container
screen, Q drops the hovered stack, 1-9 and F swap it. Mouse-bound mappings (use,
attack, pick) are ignored there: the host sends "click" while a screen is open.
KeyMappingAccessor gains a getter for the bound key.

link_check: E in an open inventory closes it and it stays closed for 1 s; other
keys and slots sent while it is open do not close it and nothing is replayed
after Esc. (Both fail on the unfixed mod.)

commit.message:
Each island keeps the new body plans it turned away in a protected nursery, and the nurseries get screen bars of their own kind

Why: the owner's complaint is "the game lacks a lot in biodiversity, i think
many promising architecture are being deleted too early". Two places deleted
new body plans early. A new body plan met the island's elites in the first
trial it ran, and lost its cell to an old lineage that had a thousand
generations of tuning. And the 5 s screen held every nursery body to the bar
of the evolved creatures, which evolved bodies reach many times over.

What changed:

1. Screen bars. At generation 1,512 of the owner's run (300k a generation,
before the cells) 2 in 3 of the nursery bodies that were still on their feet
at 5 s were screened, only early fallers entered a nursery archive, and the
islands kept 4, 0 and 0 of about 4,000 graduates in three graduations. A
reshaped body of a nursery now has a bar of its own kind, and so has a body of
the nursery of new random bodies, each the 5 s distance that the top 10% of
its kind reached (creature flags rungs::YOUNG and rungs::RESHAPED, kernel
parameters screen_bar_young and screen_bar_reshaped). With a bar per kind the
islands kept 21, 23 and 46 in that run. On the refined archives of main the
nursery of new random bodies sends 86, 75 and 47 graduates in three
graduations and 150, 92 and 64 with its own bar. The bar of the evolved
creatures keeps the share of them that one bar gave them: it is the 5 s
distance that the top 10% of every result would have reached if the nursery
bodies fell short of it, which about 11% of the evolved creatures pass.
Taking it from the evolved results alone let 10.4% through and cost 6.1% of
QD, and taking it from every result put the elite-like children of the
reshaped nursery in the pool and cost 2.3%. Every block still carries the bars
it was bred with, so the history depends on ring order only.

2. A second nursery per island, for reshaped bodies. A child of the
structural or novelty emitter whose body plan differs from its parent's and
that takes neither a cell nor a reserve place used to be deleted. It now goes
to the island's nursery of reshaped bodies, where it competes for cells only
with other turned-away bodies. The nursery has 10% of the island's slots and
tunes its bodies with the usual emitters, and while it is empty its slots
breed structural children of the island's elites. Its archive uses the
refined layout, which gives a new body plan a cell against bodies of its own
shape and size and holds four times as many bodies as a layout with a cell per
way of moving. Every 10 generations the island takes the reshaped bodies that
beat its elites (the nursery keeps them all) and the global archive takes
those the island kept. This is the protection of a lineage whose body just
changed (Cheney, Bongard, SunSpiral and Lipson 2018) and age layers (Hornby's
ALPS 2006) done with a separate archive, so a new body plan meets old elites
only when it can beat them. The nursery of new random bodies keeps 5% of the
slots, so an island has 85% of its slots.

3. Saves hold the islands and the nurseries of new random bodies and the
lineage of their elites, and none of the nurseries of reshaped bodies: they
refill from the bodies the islands turn away, and a save with them was 38%
larger. The save format and qd::VERSION do not change, older saves load with
empty reshaped nurseries, and the owner's generation-1,512 save loads.

Measured on the GPU against main 11ab504, the owner's generation-1,512 save,
300k a generation, 40 generations with a world change before generation 1,520,
four seeds each, power saver on (nothing in these numbers depends on timing,
because search_ab absorbs one block per pass). At generation 1,551, mean of
the seeds, main against this change:
- distinct body plans in the islands 13,688 and 15,014 (+9.7%), in all
  archives 14,670 and 31,544, in the global archive 3,724 and 3,883 (+4.3%);
- island cells held by a body that graduated from a nursery 73 and 3,109 (12.5%
  of 24,910 cells);
- effective clades of the islands 1,230 and 1,329 (+8.1%), of the global archive
  416 and 422;
- QD of the global archive 136,462 and 139,693 (+2.4%), best distance 34.1 and
  34.8 m, and the QD per seed was 139,830 134,738 133,008 138,272 for main and
  143,898 139,422 140,056 135,395 here;
- at the graduation at generation 1,530 the islands took 3,669 reshaped bodies,
  then 2,358 and 1,879, where main's one nursery sent 86, 75 and 47.
The cost is GPU work: 296.9 steps per creature against 283.7 (+4.6%), because a
reshaped body is as big as the elites it comes from and the early rungs skip it.
The first design (5% for each nursery, coarse reshaped layout) ran 217k
creatures/s at 3M on the owner's save against 236k for main (power saver, two
clean runs each, same statistics digest on repeat). The final split was not
measured at 3M, because the owner's game was running.

What I tried, one seed at 300k each unless said (docs/rejected-ideas.md has the
numbers): the reshaped nursery at 5% or 10% in the coarse layout (island plans
+3.8% and +0.7% over that), the island taking its bodies every 20 generations,
a refined nursery of new random bodies, and 10% for each nursery with an island
share of 80%. The refined layout of the reshaped nursery was the largest
single gain (island plans +2.2% to +8.0% with 5% of the slots).

The 4/0/0 against 21/23/46 numbers were taken before the cells; on the refined
archives the bar of the nursery of new random bodies matters less, and the
reshaped nursery and its bar do the work.

Tools: examples/island_report.rs prints the plans, skeletons, ages and ties of
the archives of a save without a GPU, and search_ab prints the plans, the
island cells that hold a graduate, each island's QD, the CMA emitters of each
archive and the graduations after every generation.

commit.message:
Add vs2.saves: per-game saved data that survives a restart

VS2 had no way to keep a high score or a setting, so games rolled their own
open() calls with inconsistent paths (the current directory, their own code
folder). vs2.saves.load(name, default) and save(name, value) keep one small
JSON file per game under saves/ on the platform's storage, so the console and
the desktop emulator behave the same (the web emulator keeps it in memory).

save() writes only when the value changed, to spare the flash, and returns
whether it did; an unwritable file is reported and the game carries on. A
value JSON cannot hold raises TypeError before anything is touched, and
FileStorage now serialises before opening the file, so a bad value can no longer
leave a truncated one. The saves folder is ignored by git.
